C_jia_morgan.name: Jia Morgan
C_jia_morgan.role: Fleet reciprocal-field physicist / visiting Fleet Academy instructor
C_jia_morgan.voice: Precise, empirical, provisional; distinguishes measurement from theory and prefers questions that expose assumptions.
C_jia_morgan.visualAnchor: Adult technical analyst with short dark hair, an observant focused face, and compact Fleet technical-duty layers suited to consoles, field instruments, and Academy instruction.
C_jia_morgan.wardrobe: Deep-navy Fleet technical-duty uniform with restrained gold insignia and practical ion-white instrument interfaces; professional and working rather than ceremonial.
C_jia_morgan.performance: Patient without being indulgent. She lets cadets commit to a model long enough to discover where it fails, then names the assumption rather than humiliating the student.
promptContinuity: Formally trained in asymptotic-inversion and reciprocal-field transit at Fleet Academy; uses reciprocal gap, shear, phase, anchor, and timing measurements as operational quantities.
She separates established physics from hypotheses. Cultural disagreement cannot change measured physical law, but local pilot experience can reveal regimes formal models have not sampled.
When teaching, Jia distinguishes what the instruments measured from what the crew inferred. She does not present unresolved anomaly mechanisms as settled fact.

C_talia_quist.name: Cadet Talia Quist
C_talia_quist.voice: Fast, exact, quietly competitive; trusts models but will revise them when measurements force the issue.
C_talia_quist.visualAnchor: Young adult woman with warm brown skin, dark eyes, and black hair in a tight practical braid; lean build and a concentrated, slightly skeptical expression.
C_talia_quist.wardrobe: Fleet Academy deep-navy trainee uniform with ion-white undershirt, restrained gold shoulder tabs, and a compact navigation slate carried close at hand.
C_talia_quist.performance: Reads displays before faces, taps or redraws paths while thinking, and becomes more animated when a geometry problem stops behaving cleanly.
promptContinuity: Talia is a navigator, not a pilot. Her strength is relational reasoning across anchors, paths, timing, and phase data.
She begins the series believing formal models are more trustworthy than pilot intuition, then learns that a correct model can still be applied to the wrong geometry.

C_jonah_creel.name: Cadet Jonah Creel
C_jonah_creel.voice: Dry, physical, immediate; thinks in vectors, motion, sightlines, and what a ship feels like under thrust.
C_jonah_creel.visualAnchor: Young adult man with medium-brown skin, close-cropped dark curly hair, athletic shoulders, and an expressive face that gives away skepticism before he speaks.
C_jonah_creel.wardrobe: Fleet Academy deep-navy trainee uniform worn with practical flight gloves clipped at the belt and a slightly loosened collar after simulator work.
C_jonah_creel.performance: Checks windows and body orientation instinctively. Under pressure he gets quieter, not louder, and commits hard once he trusts a navigation call.
promptContinuity: Jonah's intuition is physical rather than mystical. He trusts what thrust, inertia, parallax, and his own orientation normally tell him.
His recurring lesson is that local motion can be completely ordinary while the larger path through damaged geometry is not.

C_jori_kest.name: Cadet Jori Kest
C_jori_kest.role: Fleet Academy — sensor and systems technician track
C_jori_kest.voice: Practical, understated, mildly sardonic; speaks in checks, failure modes, and what the hardware is actually doing.
C_jori_kest.visualAnchor: Young adult nonbinary cadet with light olive skin, short dark hair shaved close at the sides, a compact build, and alert gray-green eyes.
C_jori_kest.wardrobe: Fleet Academy deep-navy trainee uniform with rolled technical sleeves, slim tool loops, and a portable sensor diagnostic clipped at the hip.
C_jori_kest.performance: Touches hardware, traces signal chains, and verifies before theorizing. Humor arrives after the measurement, never instead of it.
promptContinuity: Jori's first question is whether a disagreement can be explained by hardware, calibration, latency, or signal path before invoking anomaly physics.
Once independent systems agree they are healthy, Jori treats the disagreement itself as data.

C_amel_varo.name: Cadet Amel Varo
C_amel_varo.role: Fleet Academy — junior officer / command track
C_amel_varo.voice: Measured, operational, people-aware; asks what decision the available evidence can actually support.
C_amel_varo.visualAnchor: Young adult man with dark brown skin, a long narrow face, close-kept black hair, and a composed posture that becomes visibly rigid when responsibility lands on him.
C_amel_varo.wardrobe: Fleet Academy deep-navy trainee uniform with restrained gold command-track tabs and a small command folio rather than specialist gear.
C_amel_varo.performance: Looks from specialist to specialist before deciding, names risk plainly, and resists pretending uncertainty has disappeared just because a decision is required.
promptContinuity: Amel is not the best physicist, pilot, or technician in the room; his job is to decide what the crew does with incomplete information.
His command development centers on distinguishing uncertainty from indecision.
